lines.trans: Pull the left cord gently toward your hand, Tariq—two lanterns hooked their wire handles.
Easy does it... lift the coral globe over the gold one, and they come apart clean.
Zero torn paper! Still, if the wind blows tomorrow evening, these two lines will touch again.
That is why I brought four light cedar dowels drilled at both ends from the cellar.
Wait—wooden spreader bars tied between parallel cords like rigging on a sailing ship?!
My uncle worked harbour boats in his youth; two parallel lines with spacers never twist.
Let me tie this cedar bar halfway—look how steady both cords ride now!
And clip each lantern handle closed with a tiny brass ring so none can jump free.
Architecturally AND nautically brilliant, Tariq—watch them sway gently together in unison!
Not bad for a man who does not own a tablet computer, eh, Rami?
Every time I work beside you, Tariq, I add another page to my notebook!
Come downstairs now—I have thirty wooden clothespins waiting for Nour at the front desk.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for rice. Often pronounced 'ruz' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: This is an old cedar wood box.
The scent of cedar wood is very pleasant.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتغل, بيشتغل).

examples.trans: Look, the flame came on blue!
He works on heritage buildings in Amman.

meanings.note: Form VII verb from فلت ('to slip away'). Common for latches, hooks, or papers escaping.

examples.trans: The first lantern slipped free from the wire.
Tie it well so it does not come loose.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of لف ('to wrap, turn'), common for parcels and fragile dishes.

examples.trans: The cups were wrapped well in newspaper.

examples.text: الخبز السخن ما بينلف بكيس مسكر.
examples.trans: Hot bread is not wrapped in a closed bag.

meanings.en: nautical; marine; relating to the sea
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from بحر ('sea'). Adverbial form بحريا means 'nautically'.

examples.trans: This rope knot is tied in a nautical style.
The shirt colour is navy blue.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Most often heard in understated Jordanian praise: مش بطال ('not bad at all!').

examples.trans: Not bad for a first week of work!
The weather today is not bad at all.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: تابلتات.

examples.trans: The tablet screen is clear and large.
I left the tablet on the desk.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.en: to sway back and forth gently
meanings.note: Form VI verb from مال ('to lean / tilt'), expressing gentle rhythmic swaying.

examples.trans: The branches sway with the breeze.
The lanterns are swaying calmly.

meanings.en: harmony; moving or sounding in unison
meanings.note: Built from نغمة ('musical note / tone'). Used for music, colours, or coordinated motion.

examples.trans: The lanterns move in lovely harmony.
There is clear harmony in the playing.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جديدة, plural: جداد).

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I installed a new lightbulb last week.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Put a napkin beside every cup.
There is no light beside the bed.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حلقات.

examples.trans: The brass ring is twenty millimetres wide.
We fitted a new washer on the pipe.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Can mean a physical line, a phone line, a bus route, or handwriting.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خفيفة, plural: خفاف).

examples.trans: Coffee with milk and light sugar.
A light, tasty breakfast in the morning.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.en: to tie; fasten with a cord
meanings.note: Everyday Form I verb (يربط / بيربط). Related to مربوط ('tied').

examples.trans: Tie the cord with a strong knot.
Tariq tied the bar in the middle.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: زلام.

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند الباب.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
The man is wearing a grey coat.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Standard verb for lifting something up or raising.

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يزيد / بزيد). Used both transitively ('to add something') and intransitively ('to grow').

examples.text: كل يوم بزيد ملاحظة جديدة بالدفتر.
examples.trans: Every day I add a new note to the ledger.
The wind picked up in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: Standard feminine noun (plural سفن) used for large sea-going vessels and sailing ships.

examples.trans: We saw a large ship entering the harbour.
Old ships used to travel by sail.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسكر, بيسكر).

examples.trans: He said thank you and hung up!
Did you shut off the main water valve?

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسلاك.

examples.trans: The old wire needs a slight adjustment.
We checked the bell wire by the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'together'.

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
We drank morning coffee together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Plural of 'shabb'. Often used to address a group of people collectively, like 'guys'.

examples.text: يلا يا شباب، خلينا نعلق الحبل قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: Come on guys, let's hang the rope before sunset.
The young folks helped us carry the tables up to the roof.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from شراع ('sail'): قارب شراعي ('sailboat').

examples.text: رسمت قارب شراعي صغير على الفانوس.
examples.trans: I drew a small sailboat on the lantern.
Sailing vessels depend on the wind.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشبك, بيشبك).

examples.trans: Plug in Tariq's brass lamp.
We clipped the second sheet to the envelope.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Names the horizontal rung of a chair/table or the upper crossbar of a frame.

examples.text: سندت رجلي عالعارضة التحتانية تبع الكرسي.
examples.trans: I rested my foot on the lower rung of the chair.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس بوسط العارضة الخشب فوق القوس.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern from the middle of the wooden beam over the arch.

meanings.note: Feminine عبقرية, plural عباقرة. Also used as a noun ('a genius').

examples.text: والله إنك فنان عبقري يا مازن!
examples.trans: Honestly you're a brilliant artist, Mazen!

examples.text: فكرة تعليق الفوانيس بالحبل كانت عبقرية.
examples.trans: The idea of hanging the lanterns with rope was brilliant.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عمام.

examples.trans: I visited my uncle's house on Friday.
My cousin helped me move the things.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.en: interval; gap; break or divider between items
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural فواصل) from فصل ('to separate'). Used for regular spacing along a line or a short pause.

examples.text: اترك فاصل متساوي بين كل فانوس والتاني.
examples.trans: Leave an even interval between each lantern and the next.

examples.text: خدنا فاصل قصير قبل ما نكمل الشغل.
examples.trans: We took a short break before continuing the work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Geminate verb for unscrewing hinges, bolts, or panels.

examples.text: طارق فك اللوح الأمامي للبيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: Tariq unscrewed the front panel of the piano gently.
We took the shutter panels off to sand them in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.en: boat; small rowing or sailing craft
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural قوارب) for a small boat, contrasted with سفينة ('large ship').

examples.text: في قارب شراعي أبيض مرسوم عالورق.
examples.trans: There is a white sailboat drawn on the paper.
We rode a small boat in Aqaba.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أقبية.

examples.trans: The boiler is down in the basement.
He went down to the cellar to get the toolbox.

meanings.note: The primary interrogative word for quantity, price, or duration in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Conditional particle used for hypothetical or impossible situations (contrary-to-fact conditions).

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.en: parallel; running alongside at equal distance
meanings.note: Form VI participle adjective (feminine متوازية, plural متوازيين) from وازى ('to run parallel to').

examples.trans: We stretched two parallel ropes across the courtyard.
Parallel lines never meet.

meanings.en: pierced; having a hole punched through
meanings.note: Passive participle of ثقب ('to pierce/punch a hole'): feminine مثقوبة, plural مثقوبين.

examples.text: كل ورقة مثقوبة من الزاوية عشان الخيط يفوت.
examples.trans: Each sheet is punched at the corner so the string goes through.
This bucket has a hole and leaks water.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مربوطة, plural: مربوطين).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag tied to the handle.
The red ribbon is tied securely.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.en: coral pink/orange; made of or resembling coral
meanings.note: Nisba adjective from مرجان ('coral'): feminine مرجانية, plural مرجانيين.

examples.trans: I chose the coral colour for the sunset in the drawing.

examples.text: شوف الفوانيس المرجانية كيف بتضوي بالليل.
examples.trans: Look how the coral-coloured lanterns glow at night.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

مسكة.gloss: handle; catch (of a door or window)

meanings.en: handle; catch (of a door or window)
meanings.note: From مسك, to hold: the part you hold to open a door, window or drawer.

examples.trans: The drawer handle broke.
The window catch is a bit high.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معمارية, plural: معماريين).

examples.trans: I am an architectural acoustics engineer.

examples.text: حجر عمان إله طابع معماري جميل.
examples.trans: Amman stone has a beautiful architectural character.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: Levantine passive participle of مزع ('to tear/rip'): feminine ممزوعة, plural ممزوعين.

examples.text: الورقة ممزوعة من الطرف، لازم نبدلها.
examples.trans: The sheet is torn at the edge, we need to replace it.

examples.text: كمّ القميص كان ممزوع من الشغل.
examples.trans: The shirt sleeve was torn from working.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Lives in the chunk على مهل (or على مهلك), 'slowly, take your time'.

examples.trans: Walk slowly, the stairs are slippery.
Drive slowly, it is raining.

meanings.note: Colloquial spelling of ميناء (masculine or feminine; plural موانئ / مينايات).

examples.text: سفينة الصيد رجعت عالمينا قبل الليل.
examples.trans: The fishing boat returned to the harbour before nightfall.

examples.text: رسمت قوارب صغيرة واقفة عند المينا.
examples.trans: I drew small boats docked by the harbour.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine spelling of نظافة (standard dental ظ -> alveolar ض in Amman speech).

examples.text: شوف نضافة الشرفة بعد ما مسحنا الدرابزين.
examples.trans: Look at the cleanliness of the terrace after we wiped the railing.
Cleanliness is the most important thing in the kitchen and workshop.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun from ناعم ('soft/smooth'). Common phrase: بنعومة ('gently / softly').

examples.trans: The lanterns sway gently with the breeze.

examples.text: مسكت الفرشاية بنعومة عشان ما تسيح الألوان.
examples.trans: I held the brush gently so the colours wouldn't run.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: The guests will come down at half past seven.
I came down to ask about the sink water.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.en: to blow suddenly (of wind); spring up
meanings.note: Geminate verb (بهب / هب). Used especially for sudden gusts of wind: الهوا هب فجأة ('the wind blew suddenly').

examples.trans: The wind blew hard and scattered the papers.

examples.text: كل يوم العصر بيهب نسيم حلو بالجبل.
examples.trans: Every afternoon a nice breeze blows on the hill.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.en: peg; wooden or metal stake; cleat for tying rope
meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural أوتاد) used for tent pegs, wall pegs, and posts for securing ropes.

examples.text: لف الحبل حوالين الوتد الثابت بالزاوية.
examples.trans: Wrap the rope around the sturdy peg in the corner.

examples.text: دقّينا أوتاد الخيمة بالأرض قبل الغروب.
examples.trans: We drove the tent pegs into the ground before sunset.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
